title: Cluster Link Visualizer and Incident Timeline for Private Console
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Purpose: Design an interactive cluster-level "link visualizer" and an adjacent incident timeline for the Redwood Private Console. The feature helps platform engineers and SREs quickly understand cross-cluster connectivity, recent upgrades, and correlated incidents for VPC/on-prem deployments.

Scope: Deliver a high-fidelity prototype and annotated spec for the Console team covering:
- A topology canvas that visualizes clusters, cross-cluster links (peering/VPN), and traffic-health overlays (latency, packet loss indicators).
- Click-to-expand cluster cards with capacity, software version, and current active rollouts.
- An incident timeline aligned horizontally beneath the canvas that shows upgrades, outages, and scheduled maintenance with breadcrumb links to runbooks and incident pages.
- Filters for region, environment (staging/prod), and link type (peering/direct, transit).
- Lightweight quick-actions: open cluster logs, start a rollback for a rollout, open a support ticket.

UX goals:
1) Make root-cause spotting faster: visually highlight links with recent error spikes and surface correlated timeline events.
2) Minimize noise: default to aggregated view with ability to drill into per-link KPIs.
3) Keep console consistent with existing Redwood visual language (cards, chips, tokens) and accessibility standards.
4) Provide clear affordances for private/VPC-specific controls (network ACLs, routing table preview, FQDN reachability).

Design deliverables:
- Figma prototype (desktop primarily, responsive to 1280px down to 720px) with annotated interactions.
- Interaction spec (.md) for engineering: expected API endpoints, sample payloads for topology and timeline events, and recommended polling/backoff strategy.
- Accessibility notes and keyboard-first interaction map.
- Acceptance criteria and QA checklist for design handoff.

Constraints and assumptions:
- We assume the runtime/engineering team can emit a topology graph and normalized event stream. If not available, fallback to periodic snapshot ingestion.
- For early rollout, limit to clusters registered under Private control plane (not external peer-only clusters).
- Data retention for timeline events will be configured by PM and may be limited; design must handle sparse historical data gracefully.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha M: Initial concept sketch uploaded to Figma. Focused on two-pane layout: canvas + timeline. Asked ENG for topology API contract. Link: https://figma.redwood.com/file/abcd123/cluster-link-visualizer-proto
2026-03-04 - Diego A: Reviewed early prototype — flagged complexity in multi-link selection. Suggested 'focus mode' to isolate a single cluster and its immediate neighbors.

2026-03-05 - PM (Jae Park): +1 on focus mode. Requested inclusion of 'scheduled upgrades' as a distinct timeline event type. Marked customer_impact=medium and asked for supporting copy for release notes.

2026-03-06 - Eng (Maya Li): Confirmed topology API (ENG-2071) will provide nodes, links, linkMetrics, and rollouts array. Will return mocked endpoint by 2026-03-09. Also noted limits on linkMetrics resolution (30s buckets).
2026-03-08 - Design critique: Accessibility group recommended color-blind safe palettes and ensuring timeline events have textual labels on hover and a visible focus ring for keyboard navigation.

2026-03-09 - User testing (internal SREs): 6 participants, median time-to-identify-root-cause improved by ~28% in prototype tasks. Feedback: legends need to be persistent and event hover needs clearer signal. Summary: https://docs.redwood.com/ux/research/cluster-visualizer

2026-03-10 - Asha M: Updated prototype with 'isolate link' action, persistent legend, and added 'open runbook' quick-action on timeline items. Preparing design spec for handoff. GitHub PR for sample data: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1824
acceptance_criteria: Canvas renders <= 2s for up to 50 nodes in staging dataset
Timeline events align to canvas viewport and clicking an event highlights affected nodes/links
Keyboard navigation: users can tab through clusters, expand cards, and trigger quick-actions without a mouse
Design spec includes color tokens and contrast ratios meeting WCAG AA
Prototype annotated with API field mappings and sample payloads for eng handoff
